LONG-SHORT DIRECT INDEXING

Portfolio research

Compare portfolio rules, exit strategies and the timing of outside gains.

Model coverage ↗

Parameters

Illustrative annual returns and harvested losses, not historical stock prices. All strategies start with the same cash.

Inheritance and gifts

Assumption for the death scenario. Long-only holdings use full FMV basis adjustment. Short liabilities receive no automatic adjustment.

Gift wealth combines donor and recipient assets after separate taxes. It is not cash retained by the donor alone. Estate and gift taxes are excluded.

Tests $0, $1M, $3M and $5M in this year only. Searches $0–$5M for break-even against both Index and Direct Indexing.

Synthetic prices and membership rows test the software. They are not actual stocks or S&P 500 history.

One row per stock: ticker, long/short, relative weight, replacement ticker. For portfolio sampling, these rows define replacements; the membership file defines the universe.

Target 130% long / 30% short after trading fees. Harvest signals execute next close. Original-stock reentry waits more than 30 calendar days; a mapped replacement maintains the position meanwhile.

Optional for the synthetic example; required for other data. Columns: ticker, member_from, member_to, published_as_of, source_id, point_in_time_verified. Membership ends are exclusive; formation uses the start date. No genuine S&P 500 membership file is included.

Fees, financing and taxes

Annual rates except per-trade cost. Index manager fee is 0.03%; DI is 0.25% in annual studies. These are assumptions, not current quotes. Historical studies apply the advisor fee to every comparison.
